revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Build the Arcade Scoreboard
revealWordProblem.text: You are programming the scoreboard for a new arcade game. A player clears 7/8 of the level. The leaderboard must show this score as a percent, and the game engine stores it as a decimal. What percent and what decimal should the scoreboard display for 7/8? Show how you converted between all three forms.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The denominator 8 does not scale to 100 by a whole number (8 × 12 = 96, 8 × 13 = 104), so I divide instead: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, and 0.875 × 100 = 87.5%. That is the same as 87.5/100. So 7/8 = 0.875 = 87.5%. The leaderboard shows 87.5% and the game engine stores 0.875.

conceptIntro.heading: How can one value be written as a fraction, a decimal, AND a percent?
conceptIntro.intro: Equivalent forms name the same value in different ways. Percent means "out of 100," so a fraction is already a percent once its denominator is 100.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: To turn a fraction into a percent, build an equivalent fraction with a denominator of 100: ask “what do I multiply the denominator by to get 100?” and multiply the numerator by that same number. The new numerator is the percent.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: A player scored 3/4 of the points. Percent means out of 100, so I want an equivalent fraction with 100 on the bottom.
What do I multiply the denominator 4 by to get 100? 4 × 25 = 100, so my scale factor is 25.
I have to multiply the top by that same 25: 3 × 25 = 75. So 3/4 = 75/100.
75 out of 100 is 75%. And 75/100 as a decimal is 0.75, because hundredths sit two places after the point.
So 3/4 = 75/100 = 0.75 = 75%. All three name the same score.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Let's change 1/5 into a fraction out of 100, then a decimal and a percent.
What do we multiply the denominator 5 by to get 100? (20)
Now multiply the numerator by that same 20: 1 × 20 = ? (20) So 1/5 = 20/100.
20 out of 100 is what percent? (20%) And as a decimal? (0.2)

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: In the table, first build the equivalent fraction out of 100 — you find the number that turns the denominator into 100.
Then read the percent straight off the new numerator, and write the same value as a decimal.
If the denominator will not scale to 100 evenly (like 8 or 3), divide the numerator by the denominator instead, then multiply by 100.

explore.instructions: Complete the conversion table. Build the equivalent fraction out of 100 first — that column is what makes the percent easy to read.

discourse.prompt: What number did you multiply by to turn each denominator into 100, and how did that fraction out of 100 give you the percent?

approaching.instructions: Sort these values — which are greater than 50% and which are less than 50%?
hints: 50% is the same as 1/2 or 0.5 — that is your comparison line for every card.
Turn each card into a fraction out of 100 or a decimal, then ask: is it more or less than 50/100?
Try 3/4 first: 4 × 25 = 100, so multiply the top by 25 too — 3/4 = 75/100 = 0.75. Is 75/100 above or below 50/100? Sort it, then test the other cards the same way.
approaching.explanation: 50% is the same value as 0.5 and 1/2, so turning each card into a decimal makes the sort quick. 3/4 = 0.75, 0.8, 65% = 0.65, and 7/10 = 0.7 all sit above 0.5. 1/3 ≈ 0.33, 0.25, 40% = 0.4, and 2/5 = 0.4 all sit below 0.5.
approaching.explanationEs: 50% es el mismo valor que 0.5 y que 1/2, así que convertir cada tarjeta en decimal hace rápida la clasificación. 3/4 = 0.75, 0.8, 65% = 0.65 y 7/10 = 0.7 quedan todos por encima de 0.5. 1/3 ≈ 0.33, 0.25, 40% = 0.4 y 2/5 = 0.4 quedan todos por debajo de 0.5.
approaching.instructionsEs: Clasifica estos valores: ¿cuáles son mayores que 50% y cuáles son menores que 50%?
hintsEs: 50% es lo mismo que 1/2 o 0.5: esa es tu línea de comparación para cada tarjeta.
Convierte cada tarjeta en una fracción de cada 100 o en un decimal y luego pregunta: ¿es más o menos que 50/100?
Prueba primero 3/4: 4 × 25 = 100, así que multiplica también el numerador por 25 — 3/4 = 75/100 = 0.75. ¿Está 75/100 arriba o abajo de 50/100? Clasifícala y prueba las demás igual.

choiceFeedback: Try again: 5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 as well.
Build an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 — multiply the top and bottom by the same number.
hints: Percent means out of 100. What do you multiply the denominator 5 by to get 100?
5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the numerator by that same 20 to build the equivalent fraction.
3 × 20 = 60, so 3/5 = 60/100. A fraction out of 100 IS the percent.
hintsEs: Porcentaje significa de cada 100. ¿Por cuánto multiplicas el denominador 5 para llegar a 100?
5 × 20 = 100, así que multiplica el numerador por ese mismo 20 para formar la fracción equivalente.
3 × 20 = 60, entonces 3/5 = 60/100. Una fracción de cada 100 ES el porcentaje.

choiceFeedback: Double-check: 20 × 5 = 100, so the top must be multiplied by 5 too.
Scale 7/20 up to a denominator of 100 first.
hints: The denominator 20 is friendly: 20 × 5 = 100, and percents are always 'out of 100'.
Make an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 by multiplying top AND bottom by the same number.
Multiply 7/20 by 5/5: the bottom becomes 100. Whatever the top becomes is your percent.
hintsEs: El denominador 20 es amigable: 20 × 5 = 100, y los porcentajes siempre son 'de cada 100'.
Forma una fracción equivalente con denominador 100 multiplicando arriba Y abajo por el mismo número.
Multiplica 7/20 por 5/5: la parte de abajo se vuelve 100. Lo que quede arriba es tu porcentaje.

approaching.explanation: 45% means 45/100, and 45/100 written as a decimal is 0.45 (forty-five hundredths).
choiceFeedback: Divide the percent by 100, or move the decimal point left 2 places.
0.045 is forty-five THOUSANDTHS — one place too far. Percent to decimal moves the point exactly two places left.
45.0 keeps the percent's full size. Percent means 'per hundred,' so the decimal form must be much smaller — move the point two places left.
hints: Percent means 'out of 100', so 45% is the fraction 45/100.
To turn a percent into a decimal, divide by 100 — the decimal point slides two places to the LEFT.
Start at 45. and move the decimal two places left: 45 → 4.5 → where does it land after the second hop?
approaching.explanationEs: 45% significa 45/100, y 45/100 escrito como decimal es 0.45 (cuarenta y cinco centésimos).
hintsEs: Porcentaje significa 'de cada 100', así que 45% es la fracción 45/100.
Para convertir un porcentaje en decimal, divide entre 100: el punto decimal se desliza dos lugares a la IZQUIERDA.
Empieza en 45. y mueve el punto dos lugares a la izquierda: 45 → 4.5 → ¿dónde cae después del segundo salto?

approaching.explanation: 0.75 = 75/100. Simplify by dividing both by 25: 75÷25 = 3 and 100÷25 = 4. So 0.75 = 3/4.
choiceFeedback: Think: 0.75 = 75/100. Can you simplify that fraction?
Try converting the decimal to a fraction with 100 in the denominator.
hints: 0.75 is read 'seventy-five hundredths' — the place value tells you the denominator.
Write the decimal as a fraction over 100, then simplify by dividing top and bottom by a common factor.
Write 75/100, then divide both the 75 and the 100 by 25 to simplify.
approaching.explanationEs: 0.75 = 75/100. Simplifica dividiendo ambos entre 25: 75 ÷ 25 = 3 y 100 ÷ 25 = 4. Entonces 0.75 = 3/4.
hintsEs: 0.75 se lee 'setenta y cinco centésimas': el valor posicional te dice el denominador.
Escribe el decimal como fracción sobre 100 y luego simplifica dividiendo arriba y abajo entre un factor común.
Escribe 75/100 y luego divide tanto el 75 como el 100 entre 25 para simplificar.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the digits as the percent
workedExample.work: The numerator is 3 and the denominator is 5, so the student writes 35%.
workedExample.labelEs: Lee los dígitos como el porcentaje
workedExample.workEs: El numerador es 3 y el denominador es 5, así que el estudiante escribe 35%.

approaching.correctWork: You cannot just read the digits. Percent means out of 100, so build the equivalent fraction: 5 × 20 = 100, and 3 × 20 = 60. So 3/5 = 60/100 = 0.6 = 60%, not 35%.
hints: Do the digits 3 and 5 tell you how many parts out of 100?
approaching.explanation: The two digits of a fraction are not the two digits of a percent. Percent means out of 100, so rewrite 3/5 with a denominator of 100: multiply the bottom by 20 to reach 100, and the top by that same 20. That gives 3/5 = 60/100 = 60%, not 35%.
approaching.explanationEs: Las dos cifras de una fracción no son las dos cifras de un por ciento. Porcentaje significa de cada 100, así que reescribe 3/5 con denominador 100: multiplica abajo por 20 para llegar a 100 y arriba por ese mismo 20. Eso da 3/5 = 60/100 = 60%, no 35%.
approaching.correctWorkEs: No puedes simplemente leer los dígitos. Porcentaje significa de cada 100, así que construye la fracción equivalente: 5 × 20 = 100, y 3 × 20 = 60. Así que 3/5 = 60/100 = 0.6 = 60%, no 35%.

onLevel.label: Place each value on the number line: A = 3/8, B = 0.6, C = 85%
hints: The three values are in different forms (fraction, decimal, percent). A number line needs them all in ONE form.
Convert each value to a decimal between 0 and 1, then place it.
Start with A = 3/8. No whole number times 8 gives 100 (8 × 12 = 96, 8 × 13 = 104), so divide instead: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. Now do C: 85% is already 85/100 = 0.85.
onLevel.explanation: A number line can only hold one form at a time, so convert all three values to decimals: A = 3/8 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375, B = 0.6 is already a decimal, and C = 85% = 85 ÷ 100 = 0.85. That puts A between 0.3 and 0.4 (closer to 0.4), B exactly at 0.6, and C between 0.8 and 0.9.
onLevel.explanationEs: Una recta numérica solo puede manejar una forma a la vez, así que convierte los tres valores a decimales: A = 3/8 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375, B = 0.6 ya es decimal, y C = 85% = 85 ÷ 100 = 0.85. Así A queda entre 0.3 y 0.4 (más cerca de 0.4), B queda exactamente en 0.6 y C queda entre 0.8 y 0.9.

onLevel.stem: A game shows your score as 7/8 complete. What percent is that?
onLevel.explanation: 8 does not scale to 100 by a whole number, so divide: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, and 0.875 × 100 = 87.5%. That is 87.5 out of 100.
choiceFeedback: 8 will not scale to 100 evenly — divide 7 by 8, then multiply by 100.
Convert the fraction to a decimal first.
88% is the rounded version, but this score converts exactly. Divide 7 by 8 and keep every decimal place — the percent is not a whole number.
hints: Try the out-of-100 move first: is there a whole number you can multiply 8 by to get exactly 100?
There isn't (8 × 12 = 96, 8 × 13 = 104), so use the backup method: divide the numerator by the denominator.
7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, which is 87.5/100 — slide the decimal two places right to read the percent.
onLevel.stemEs: Un juego muestra tu puntaje como 7/8 completado. ¿Qué porcentaje es eso?
onLevel.explanationEs: 8 no escala a 100 con un número entero, así que divide: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, y 0.875 × 100 = 87.5%. Eso es 87.5 de cada 100.
hintsEs: Prueba primero el paso de cada 100: ¿hay un número entero por el que puedas multiplicar 8 para llegar exactamente a 100?
No lo hay (8 × 12 = 96, 8 × 13 = 104), así que usa el método de respaldo: divide el numerador entre el denominador.
7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, que es 87.5/100; desliza el punto dos lugares a la derecha para leer el porcentaje.

onLevel.instructions: Complete each row. Build the fraction out of 100 first — that column hands you the percent.
hints: Each row gives you ONE form. Percent means out of 100, so try to rewrite each fraction with a denominator of 100.
Fraction → percent: scale to /100 when you can (2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50 all work). If the denominator will not reach 100 (8, 3, 7), divide instead and then multiply by 100.
onLevel.explanation: Percent means out of 100, so scale each fraction to a denominator of 100 when you can: 2/5 = 40/100 = 0.4 = 40%, and 90% = 90/100 = 0.9 = 9/10. When the denominator will not reach 100 with a whole number, divide instead: 1/8 = 0.125 = 12.5%, and 5/8 = 0.625 = 62.5%.
onLevel.explanationEs: Porcentaje significa de cada 100, así que escala cada fracción a denominador 100 cuando puedas: 2/5 = 40/100 = 0.4 = 40% y 90% = 90/100 = 0.9 = 9/10. Cuando el denominador no llega a 100 con un número entero, divide: 1/8 = 0.125 = 12.5% y 5/8 = 0.625 = 62.5%.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Completa cada fila convirtiendo a las tres formas.
hintsEs: Cada fila te da UNA forma. Porcentaje significa de cada 100, así que intenta reescribir cada fracción con denominador 100.
Fracción → porcentaje: escala a /100 cuando puedas (2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 25 y 50 funcionan). Si el denominador no llega a 100 (8, 3, 7), divide y luego multiplica por 100.

onLevel.instructions: Order these values from least to greatest by sorting them into the correct position.
hints: Two cards already show their decimals in parentheses — you only need to convert 0.35 and 55% to compare all five.
Rewrite every card as a decimal, then order the decimals from smallest to largest.
55% = 0.55. Now line up 0.20, 0.35, 0.40, 0.55, 0.75 and drag each card to its position.
onLevel.explanation: Rewriting every card as a decimal makes them comparable: 1/5 = 0.20, then 0.35, then 2/5 = 0.40, then 55% = 0.55, then 3/4 = 0.75. Those decimals run smallest to largest in exactly that order, so the cards land 1/5, 0.35, 2/5, 55%, 3/4.
onLevel.explanationEs: Reescribir cada tarjeta como decimal permite compararlas: 1/5 = 0.20, luego 0.35, luego 2/5 = 0.40, luego 55% = 0.55 y por último 3/4 = 0.75. Esos decimales van de menor a mayor justo en ese orden, así que las tarjetas quedan 1/5, 0.35, 2/5, 55%, 3/4.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Ordena estos valores de menor a mayor colocándolos en la posición correcta.
hintsEs: Dos tarjetas ya muestran su decimal entre paréntesis: solo necesitas convertir 0.35 y 55% para comparar las cinco.
Reescribe cada tarjeta como decimal y luego ordena los decimales de menor a mayor.
55% = 0.55. Ahora alinea 0.20, 0.35, 0.40, 0.55, 0.75 y arrastra cada tarjeta a su lugar.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Divide the bottom by the top
workedExample.labelEs: Divide el de abajo entre el de arriba

onLevel.correctWork: The student divided in the wrong order. To turn a fraction into a decimal, divide the TOP by the bottom: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, then × 100 → 62.5%. So 5/8 = 0.625 = 62.5%. (A check: 5/8 is less than 1, so the percent must be under 100%, never 160%.)
hints: Is 5/8 more or less than one whole? Then can its percent be over 100%?
8 will not scale to 100 evenly, so divide the numerator by the denominator: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, which is 62.5/100 → 62.5%.
onLevel.explanation: The fraction bar means numerator ÷ denominator, so this division is upside down. It should be 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, and 0.625 × 100 = 62.5%. A quick check catches it: 5/8 is less than one whole, so its percent must be under 100% — 160% was impossible.
onLevel.explanationEs: La barra de fracción significa numerador ÷ denominador, así que esta división está al revés. Debe ser 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, y 0.625 × 100 = 62.5%. Una comprobación rápida lo detecta: 5/8 es menor que un entero, así que su por ciento tiene que ser menor que 100%; 160% era imposible.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante dividió en el orden equivocado. Para convertir una fracción en decimal, divide el de ARRIBA entre el de abajo: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, luego × 100 → 62.5%. Así que 5/8 = 0.625 = 62.5%. (Una comprobación: 5/8 es menor que 1, así que el porcentaje debe estar por debajo de 100%, nunca 160%.)

extending.title: Find the Conversion Error

workedExample.label: Divide numerator by denominator
workedExample.labelEs: Divide el numerador entre el denominador

hints: 2 ÷ 3 doesn't terminate — is 0.67 the exact decimal?
0.67 is rounded. The precise decimal is 0.666... (repeating), making the percent 66.7% or 66⅔%.
extending.explanation: The division is set up the right way, but 2 ÷ 3 does not end — it gives 0.666... repeating. Writing 0.67 rounds the value, so the percent it produces (67%) is rounded too. The exact answer is 66.7% or 66⅔%.
extending.explanationEs: La división está planteada correctamente, pero 2 ÷ 3 no termina: da 0.666... periódico. Escribir 0.67 redondea el valor, así que el por ciento que resulta (67%) también queda redondeado. La respuesta exacta es 66.7% o 66⅔%.

extending.prompt: A student says 3/8 is greater than 40% because 3 and 8 are bigger numbers than 4 and 0. Is the student correct? Convert both values to the same form and explain.
extending.sentenceFrame: The student is ___ because 3/8 = ___ = ___%, which is ___ than 40%.
extending.hint: Convert 3/8 and 40% to the same form (both fractions or both percents) so you can compare them fairly.
hints: Bigger digits do NOT mean a bigger value — 3/8 and 40% can only be compared in the same form.
You can put 40% in fraction form instantly — it is 40/100. Now get 3/8 out of 100: check whether 8 scales to 100 by a whole number.
8 does not scale to 100, so divide: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375 = 37.5/100 = 37.5%. Compare that with 40/100.
extending.explanation: Bigger-looking digits do not mean a bigger value — the two amounts have to be in the same form before you compare them. Converting the fraction gives 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375, which is 37.5%. Since 37.5% is less than 40%, the student is not correct: 3/8 is the smaller value.
extending.explanationEs: Que las cifras se vean más grandes no significa que el valor sea mayor: las dos cantidades tienen que estar en la misma forma antes de compararlas. Al convertir la fracción se obtiene 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375, que es 37.5%. Como 37.5% es menor que 40%, el estudiante no tiene razón: 3/8 es el valor más pequeño.
extending.promptEs: Un estudiante dice que 3/8 es mayor que 40% porque 3 y 8 son números más grandes que 4 y 0. ¿Tiene razón? Convierte los dos valores a la misma forma y explica.
hintsEs: Dígitos más grandes NO significan mayor valor: 3/8 y 40% solo se pueden comparar en la misma forma.
Puedes poner 40% en forma de fracción de inmediato: es 40/100. Ahora pon 3/8 de cada 100: revisa si 8 escala a 100 con un número entero.
8 no escala a 100, así que divide: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375 = 37.5/100 = 37.5%. Compáralo con 40/100.

extending.label: Place 1/3, 0.4, and 38% on the number line. Which is greatest?
hints: All three values must become decimals before you can place or compare them: 1/3, 0.4, and 38%.
38% is already 38/100 = 0.38. 1/3 will not scale to 100 (3 × 33 = 99), so divide: it repeats, 0.333... Then compare the three decimals.
Place 1/3 at about 0.333 first. Then convert 38% to a decimal and see where it lands compared to 0.333 and 0.4.
extending.explanation: Convert all three to decimals before placing them: 1/3 = 0.333... (repeating), 0.4 is already a decimal, and 38% = 0.38. On the line they fall in the order 1/3 ≈ 0.333, then 38% = 0.38, then 0.4 — so 0.4 is the greatest, even though the three values look very different in their original forms.
extending.explanationEs: Convierte los tres a decimales antes de ubicarlos: 1/3 = 0.333... (periódico), 0.4 ya es decimal y 38% = 0.38. En la recta quedan en el orden 1/3 ≈ 0.333, luego 38% = 0.38 y luego 0.4, así que 0.4 es el mayor, aunque los tres valores se vean muy distintos en su forma original.

optionalActivity.name: Percent Conversion Puzzle Tiles
optionalActivity.intro: Power up your arcade scoreboard by snapping each fraction, decimal, and percent tile into its matching slot!

optional.stem: Your arcade scoreboard reads 0.25 of the level cleared. What percent and fraction match this score?
optional.explanation: Move the decimal two places: 0.25 = 25%. As a fraction, 0.25 = 25/100 = 1/4.
choiceFeedback: Remember: multiply the decimal by 100, or move the decimal point right 2 places.
Check your conversion — 0.25 as a percent should be higher.
Not quite. Move the decimal two places: 0.25 = ___%.
optional.stemEs: El marcador de tu arcade indica 0.25 del nivel completado. ¿Qué porcentaje y qué fracción corresponden a este puntaje?
optional.explanationEs: Mueve el punto decimal dos lugares: 0.25 = 25%. Como fracción, 0.25 = 25/100 = 1/4.
hints: A decimal, a percent, and a fraction can all name the same amount — percent simply means “out of 100”.
To turn a decimal into a percent, multiply by 100 (move the decimal point two places right). To turn it into a fraction, read the decimal using place-value words.
0.25 reads as twenty-five hundredths, so start the fraction as 25/100 — then move the decimal two places for the percent and simplify the fraction.
hintsEs: Un decimal, un porcentaje y una fracción pueden nombrar la misma cantidad: porcentaje significa simplemente «de cada 100».
Para convertir un decimal en porcentaje, multiplica por 100 (mueve el punto decimal dos lugares a la derecha). Para convertirlo en fracción, lee el decimal con palabras de valor posicional.
0.25 se lee veinticinco centésimos, así que empieza la fracción como 25/100; después mueve el punto dos lugares para el porcentaje y simplifica la fracción.

optional.stem: A player powered up 3/5 of the energy bar. Which decimal and percent name the same amount?
choiceFeedback: Scale 3/5 to a denominator of 100, then read the decimal and percent.
Your decimal is right, but you moved the decimal one place for the percent. A percent is per 100, so move two.
Try building the equivalent fraction out of 100 first.
optional.stemEs: Un jugador cargó 3/5 de la barra de energía. ¿Qué decimal y qué porcentaje nombran la misma cantidad?
hints: Percent means out of 100, so rewrite 3/5 with 100 on the bottom.
What do you multiply 5 by to get 100? Multiply the numerator by that same number.
5 × 20 = 100 and 3 × 20 = 60, so 3/5 = 60/100. Read the percent off the top, then write 60/100 as a decimal.
hintsEs: Porcentaje significa de cada 100, así que reescribe 3/5 con 100 abajo.
¿Por cuánto multiplicas 5 para llegar a 100? Multiplica el numerador por ese mismo número.
5 × 20 = 100 y 3 × 20 = 60, así que 3/5 = 60/100. Lee el porcentaje arriba y luego escribe 60/100 como decimal.

optional.label: Match each arcade score tile to its equal fraction, decimal, and percent.
optional.explanation: Each score tile and its match are the same value in different clothes: 4/5 = 80/100 = 0.8 = 80%, 9/10 = 90/100 = 0.9 = 90%, 1/2 = 50/100 = 0.5 = 50%, and 1/4 = 25/100 = 0.25 = 25%. Scaling a fraction to a denominator of 100 gives you its percent and its decimal at the same time.
optional.explanationEs: Cada ficha de puntaje y su pareja son el mismo valor con distinta ropa: 4/5 = 80/100 = 0.8 = 80%, 9/10 = 90/100 = 0.9 = 90%, 1/2 = 50/100 = 0.5 = 50% y 1/4 = 25/100 = 0.25 = 25%. Escalar una fracción a denominador 100 te da su porcentaje y su decimal al mismo tiempo.
hints: Every score tile has exactly one match that shows the SAME value written as a decimal and a percent.
Rewrite each fraction with a denominator of 100 — multiply the top and bottom by the same number. The new numerator is the percent.
Start with 4/5: 5 × 20 = 100, so 4 × 20 = 80. That is 80/100 — now find the card showing that value.
hintsEs: Cada ficha de puntaje tiene exactamente una pareja que muestra el MISMO valor escrito como decimal y como por ciento.
Reescribe cada fracción con denominador 100: multiplica arriba y abajo por el mismo número. El nuevo numerador es el porcentaje.
Empieza con 4/5: 5 × 20 = 100, así que 4 × 20 = 80. Eso es 80/100; ahora busca la tarjeta con ese valor.
optional.labelEs: Une cada casilla de puntaje del arcade con su fracción, decimal y porcentaje equivalentes.

optional.instructions: Sort each arcade tile into the form it is already written in.
optional.explanation: This sort is about how each tile is WRITTEN, not how big it is. A fraction shows a numerator over a denominator (2/5 and 7/10), a decimal shows a decimal point (0.3 and 0.85), and a percent carries the % symbol (70% and 15%). The very same value could appear in any of the three forms.
optional.explanationEs: Esta clasificación se trata de cómo está ESCRITA cada ficha, no de qué tan grande es. Una fracción muestra un numerador sobre un denominador (2/5 y 7/10), un decimal muestra un punto decimal (0.3 y 0.85) y un por ciento lleva el símbolo % (70% y 15%). Un mismo valor podría aparecer en cualquiera de las tres formas.
hints: You are sorting by the FORM each tile is written in, not by its value — no converting is needed here.
Look for the giveaway mark on each tile: a fraction bar, a decimal point, or a % symbol.
Take the tile 2/5: it shows one number over another with a fraction bar. Which pile does that mark point to?
hintsEs: Estás clasificando por la FORMA en que está escrita cada ficha, no por su valor; aquí no hace falta convertir nada.
Busca la marca delatora de cada ficha: una barra de fracción, un punto decimal o el símbolo %.
Toma la ficha 2/5: muestra un número sobre otro con una barra de fracción. ¿A qué grupo apunta esa marca?
optional.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada casilla del arcade según la forma en la que ya está escrita.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — Find the Decimal-to-Percent Mistake
optional.correctWork: To change a decimal to a percent, multiply by 100 (move the decimal two places RIGHT): 0.4 × 100 = 40. So 0.4 = 40%, not 4%.
hints: Which way does the decimal move when you go from a decimal to a percent — left or right?
Going decimal → percent means multiply by 100, so the point moves two places right: 0.4 becomes 40%, not 4%.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: encuentra el error de decimal a por ciento
optional.explanation: Going from a decimal to a percent means multiplying by 100, which moves the decimal point two places to the RIGHT. Moving it left divides instead, which is why 0.4 turned into 0.04. Done correctly, 0.4 × 100 = 40, so 0.4 = 40%.
optional.explanationEs: Pasar de decimal a por ciento significa multiplicar por 100, lo que mueve el punto decimal dos lugares a la DERECHA. Moverlo a la izquierda divide en vez de multiplicar, y por eso 0.4 se convirtió en 0.04. Hecho correctamente, 0.4 × 100 = 40, así que 0.4 = 40%.
optional.correctWorkEs: Para cambiar un decimal a porcentaje, multiplica por 100 (mueve el decimal dos lugares a la DERECHA): 0.4 × 100 = 40. Así que 0.4 = 40%, no 4%.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percents is treating the numerator and denominator as the percent's digits — turning 3/5 into "35%" by just reading the 3 and the 5. Percent means out of 100, so the fix is to build an equivalent fraction with denominator 100: 5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 too — 3/5 = 60/100 = 60%. A second version of this mistake is scaling only ONE part of the fraction (writing 3/5 = 3/100 or 60/5). Whatever you multiply the denominator by, you must multiply the numerator by the same number. When a denominator will not reach 100 evenly (8, 3, 7), divide the numerator by the denominator instead and then multiply by 100.

diagram.title: 3/5 Off a $40 Game
diagram.caption: Split $40 into 5 equal $8 parts: 3 of the 5 parts are taken off, so 3/5 = 60% = $24 off, leaving 2 parts = $16 to pay.

connect.scenario: A store has a clearance sale: 'Everything 3/5 off!' Your friend says that means 35% off. Another friend says it's 60% off. The original price of a game is $40.
connect.promptQuestion: Who is correct, and how much would the game cost on sale?
connect.prompt: The friend who said ___% is correct because 3/5 = ___ = ___%. The sale price is $___.

check.stem: '3/5 off' means 3 of the 5 equal parts come off the price. Which friend is right?
check.explanation: 3/5 off is 60% off. Percent means out of 100, so scale 3/5 to a denominator of 100: 5 × 20 = 100 and 3 × 20 = 60, giving 60/100 = 60%. Reading the digits 3 and 5 as '35%' ignores what the fraction means.
3/5 = 60/100, and 60 hundredths is written 0.6. You can also divide: 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6.

check.stem: The game costs $40 and 3/5 comes off. How much is taken off?
check.explanation: Split $40 into 5 equal parts of $8. Three of those parts come off: 3 × $8 = $24. That matches 60% of $40 = $24.

check.stem: So what do you actually pay for the game?
check.explanation: You keep the other 2 of the 5 parts: 2 × $8 = $16. Check it: $40 − $24 = $16.

connect.modelAnswer: The friend who said 60% is correct. 3/5 = 60/100 = 0.6 = 60%, because 5 × 20 = 100 so 3 × 20 = 60. On a $40 game that is $24 off, so the sale price is $16. The friend who said 35% just read the digits 3 and 5 instead of building a fraction out of 100.

exitTicket.stem: Which shows 0.45 as a fraction and a percent?
choiceFeedback: Try converting 0.45 to a fraction and percent differently.
Check: 0.45 as a fraction should be 45/100, and as a percent is 45%.
Your fraction 9/20 is right — the percent is what slipped. Converting 0.45 to a percent moves the decimal two places right, not one.
hints: 0.45 is 'forty-five hundredths' — that phrase hands you both the fraction AND the percent.
Write 0.45 over 100 as a fraction and simplify; for the percent, multiply the decimal by 100. Check that a choice matches BOTH.
Start with 45/100 and divide top and bottom by 5. Then compute 0.45 × 100 for the percent, and match both parts.
